# tests/fixtures/replays/

Replay fixtures for `tests.fakes.FakeTransport`. Each file is one agent reply,
keyed by the session-key suffix the runner builds:

```
<slug>-<phase>-<prompt>[-<slot>]-v<N>.json      e.g. demo-review-32-v1.json
<slug>-<phase>-<prompt>-v<N>.turn<K>.json       the K-th turn on that session
```

`.turn<K>` exists because a correction turn deliberately reuses the session key:
it is how a test scripts "bad reply, then corrected reply" for the same call.

## Three checked-in examples

| file | what it shows |
|---|---|
| `demo-p1-04-v1.json` | a drafting reply: `## Deliverable` with the H3 sections the prompt named, `## Rationale`, `## Assumptions`, `## Open Questions`, then the closing `json` envelope. The Terminology Table here is what Gate 1 locks. |
| `demo-review-32-v1.json` | a review reply: `## Findings`, `## Corrections`, and a `findings[]` envelope carrying one critical novelty finding - the one that drives the loop-back in `test_runner_flow.py`. |
| `demo-package-x-gate-brief-gate-1-v1.json` | a prose reply: plain markdown, no envelope. |

## The rest are generated

`test_runner_flow.py` and `test_cli.py` replay ~75 calls. Hand-writing that many
markdown replies would be 75 chances to get the output contract subtly wrong, and
every one would need re-editing when the contract changed. They are generated
instead, into `tmp_path`, by `tests/replay_builder.py`, from each prompt's own
`kind` and `deliverable_sections` - so a fixture is valid by construction and a
contract change surfaces as a test failure rather than as stale files.

The three above are checked in so the *shape* stays reviewable by eye, and they
are regenerated by the same builder:

```python
from tests.replay_builder import Scenario, materialise, fixture_key, novelty_finding

materialise(playbook, out_dir, Scenario(slug="demo", max_version=1))
```

A recorded live run writes the same format: `FakeTransport(mode="record",
inner=AutoTransport(...))` freezes a real smoke run into a regression suite.
